decisions.why: MWE's own top-level division name is laboratory consumables directly; the company describes itself as a pre-analytical medical device maker (specimen collection swabs and media), matching the vocabulary's 'Laboratory consumables' type exactly.
specimen-collection swab/gel products (e.g. transport media) are laboratory consumables, not diagnostic equipment or point-of-care testing devices.
bacteria specimen-collection swabs and transport media (e.g. Isolation Transwab, Sigma-VCM) are laboratory consumables used to collect and transport samples for lab analysis.
viral specimen-collection/transport media (e.g. Sigma-MM) are laboratory consumables, the same class as the bacteria/liquid/gel collection divisions.
liquid specimen-collection buffers/diluents (e.g. Butterfield Buffer) are laboratory consumables used in sample preparation.
the swab range (e.g. Forensic Swab Range, Flock Range) is specimen-collection consumables, the core of MWE's own catalogue.
products in this division (e.g. Enviro-Kit Listeria) are environmental/infection-screening specimen kits, consumables for laboratory testing rather than PPE or clinical treatment devices.
environmental sampling media (e.g. Letheen Broth, NRSII Range) are laboratory consumables for environmental microbiology testing.
food/pharma testing media (e.g. Maximum Recovery Diluent, Buffer Peptone Water) are laboratory consumables for microbiological testing, the same product class as MWE's other divisions.
forensic specimen-collection products (e.g. Sigma-Virocult) are laboratory consumables for sample collection, not forensic equipment.

the one product in this division (Amnicator, an amniotic fluid test kit) is a specimen-collection/test consumable, consistent with MWE's business as a laboratory consumables manufacturer rather than a women's health device maker.
